body:
Thanks for reporting this! I think it's caused by the newline in this module wrapping code https://github.com/loadimpact/k6/blob/c00a85bfea21d748f0f9d11fdbc326087f34c411/js/initcontext.go#L203

I guess we can remove the first `\n` without any issues, so that the line numbers match. But the offsets in a single line will still be off, and I think the only way to fix that is either refactor our module importing code, or add and support source maps (https://github.com/loadimpact/k6/issues/1789). And we shouldn't remove the second `\n` above, since scripts ending with a `// comment` will break the hack... :sweat_smile:

issue.title: Fix line numbers in imports

repository.name: k6
repository.description: A modern load testing tool, using Go and JavaScript

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0

issue.body:
Because of the way we [wrap imports](https://github.com/loadimpact/k6/blob/8e932587c51de324adc52da5bcbf75b217ea26c7/js/initcontext.go#L183), we add an additional 1 to all line numbers. (this is not true for the main script because it special ... for now). This is somewhat annoying and definitely problematic in big scripts when the error is cryptic to begin with. 
We should be able to utilize [sourcemaps](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1U1RGAehQwRypUTovF1KRlpiOFze0b-_2gc6fAH0KY0k/edit?hl=en_US&pli=1&pli=1) given that [goja supports](https://godoc.org/github.com/dop251/goja#NewSrcFile) them and we already have some code that [reads them](https://github.com/loadimpact/k6/blob/8e932587c51de324adc52da5bcbf75b217ea26c7/js/compiler/compiler.go#L115-L121) even though they were [disabled](https://github.com/loadimpact/k6/commit/31819e6ffe966fc247f58d3e717e41037068747a) and I can't find them ever being used ... ;(

I can't tell for sure as it's a long time ago and I don't have the time to get into my original script again, but I'm 51% sure the actual error line was not in the near vicinity of the line given in the error trace.

Got it!
I wondered why not more people are complaining about this. Wondered if it might be that I modularized out the huge wall of functions into a module that I import into main. 
And indeed, if a module is 'too' long, the discrepancy between the actual error line and line reported in the stack becomes more than just 1 line.

### Example:
#### stacktrace_linenumbers.js
```javascript
import * as module1 from "./module1.js"

export default function(){
//    throw "exception in line 4"
    module1.f2()
    console.log("in default")
}
```
#### module1.js
```javascript

    throw "exception in line 2"
    console.log("in f1")
}

    console.log("in f2")
```
